label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
output:
To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: p05
Cc: none
Subject: none

Mick, this must not happen: please don’t go into no. 43 at 9 with the props, and please don’t take your lad in either. I’m a chartered structural engineer with IStructE, but this is not a commission, I’ve no professional indemnity cover for free advice, and I’m speaking only as a neighbour who looked from the pavement at about 7 this morning.

What I saw: about 1.2m of no. 41’s stack is still standing and leaning towards 43. The pots are gone and the mortar at the base is visibly washed out. With gusts of 50mph forecast again this afternoon, it could go at any time. No. 43’s front roof slope has a hole roughly 2–3 square metres, so there is likely debris in the front bedroom. There’s a stepped crack in the brickwork from above the bay window up to the first-floor window cill, 5–10mm wide. The brickwork above the bay looks to have dropped by about 20mm. I can’t see the lintel because of the render. There are loose slates along the 43/45 gutter line directly over the footway.

Propping under a holed roof, with a loose stack above, is the worst place to stand. The floors may be loaded with debris and nobody knows how the weight is being carried now. A loft inspection from inside 43 is also a no.

JoJo, your cousin isn’t wrong that Victorian terraces are robust in general, but this is a damaged one. Different thing.

Priya, the pavement is not safe to use until the council has been. Their tape is only across your front garden, not the footway. Dangerous structures out of hours goes through the council’s main number; they already know, but nobody has closed the footway. Please chase that. Everyone should walk on the other side of the road until then, especially the school run.

Mrs Doherty: it isn’t my decision, and I can’t assess inside 45 from the street. But I wouldn’t sleep in the front room tonight, and I think she should go to family until 45 has been checked. The stack from 41 sits on the 41/43 party wall, not 45, and 45’s front elevation looks undamaged from outside—but that is not an inspection.
